events.title: Democratisation: closed autocracy to electoral autocracy
events.detail: Derived from a change in the Regimes of the World classification, which is itself built from V-Dem expert ratings. It marks the year a country crossed a threshold, not a specific law or decision.
events.source: derived: Regimes of the World / V-Dem
events.contested: Threshold classifications move in a single step, so the date reflects when a gradual change crossed a line rather than when it began. Read the continuous V-Dem indices alongside this to see the underlying trend.

events.title: Inflation crossed 50% (reached 59%)
events.detail: Consumer price inflation rose from 27.9% to 58.9%, crossing the 50% threshold.
events.source: derived: World Bank consumer price inflation
events.contested: The 50% line is a convention, not a natural boundary. Official inflation statistics are also among the most manipulated numbers governments publish, so the true figure may be higher than the one recorded here.

events.title: NAFTA enters into force
events.detail: The North American Free Trade Agreement phased out most tariffs between Mexico, the United States and Canada.
events.contested: Manufacturing exports and FDI rose substantially; agricultural employment fell and convergence with US income levels did not materialise as projected. Effects differ so sharply between northern and southern Mexico that national aggregates obscure more than they show.
events.refs: ["North American Free Trade Agreement (1992), entered into force 1 January 1994"]

events.title: Tequila crisis - peso devaluation
events.detail: An attempt to widen the peso's trading band triggered capital flight, forcing a float and a US-led support package of roughly US$50bn.
events.contested: A defining case in the literature on pegged exchange rates and short-term dollar-linked debt. Whether the trigger was political instability, monetary policy or the tesobono structure is still argued.
